assessment: The paper provides a detailed experimental and theoretical framework for engineering thermal reservoirs with tunable temperature and dissipation rate in a trapped-ion spin-boson simulator. It includes quantitative controls (heating rate, cooling rate, bath temperature, donor-acceptor energy gap), readouts (average phonon number, transfer rate, donor population), and mechanisms (Lindblad master equation, phonon dynamics, charge-transfer and two-mode exciton transfer models). The source supports multiple numeric claims with explicit equations, parameter values, and uncertainties, enabling the construction of an interactive experiment. However, some quantities are reported as fitted parameters or theoretical predictions without explicit experimental manipulation, and the resolution of readouts is not specified. The case is authoring-ready as it contains at least one numeric control, one numeric readout, one quantitative mechanism, and an objective source-grounded response within an explicit domain.

paper_scope: The paper proposes and demonstrates an experimental scheme to engineer thermal baths with independently tunable temperatures and dissipation rates for motional modes of a trapped-ion system. It benchmarks the protocol by realizing out-of-equilibrium dynamics of a charge-transfer model at different temperatures and studies local-temperature effects in a two-mode vibrationally assisted exciton transfer system. The work includes theory, experimental setup, control demonstrations, and applications to LVC models.
